newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks flat in morning after 12,000 test.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks flat in morning after 12,000 test.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks soared to a brief test of the 12,000 level in early Thursday morning trade, before pulling back to trend sideways and gather momentum for a full breach of this important psychological resistance level, analysts said.
"We are likely to see the market consolidate at this level, said Francis Wu, institutional sales manager at South China Securities. "The market is not that strong this morning."
The Hang Seng Index was trading 2.34 points up at 11,954.22, after briefly rising to 12,004.33 at the start of trading. Turnover was an active HK$1.07 billion after 30 minutes of trade.
The Hang Seng last traded above 12,000 on February 4, 1994, when it hit a high of 12,186.80 and closed at 12,157.57. It opened below 12,000 the following trading session.
The index is likely to challenge all time highs around the 12,500 level by the end of the year, said South China's Wu.
Most brokers tended to be cautiously optimistic.
"I'm still bullish on the market, but I think it has risen too fast. It should consolidate at this level," said Priscilla Ng, executive director at CEF GC Brokerage.
"We still have some concerns over interest rates, Ng added.
Recent market leaders were viewed as overbought.
"I'm on the sidelines, not buying property stocks, but selective red chips, said Ng.
Finance counters again led the market. HSBC rose ued its strong bull run, rising HK$1.50 to HK$145.50, another all-time high.
Cheung Kong also rose to an all-time high of HK$61.00 before easing back to HK$60.50. Henderson Land was the most actively traded issue at the open, holding steady at HK$66.00.

Sun Hung Kai Properties lost HK$0.50 to HK$81.25. The company reported a 6.5 percent rise in earnings for the year ended 30 June, in line with analysts' expectations. However, brokers viewed the stock as expensive.
"It is a long-term buy, but expensive at this level," said CEF's N"It is a long-term buy, but expensive at this level," said CEF's Ng.
First-tier red chips, CITIC Pacific and Guangdong Investment, continued to perform well, both hitting new all time highs.
CITIC Pacific jumped HK$0.70 to HK$35.80, a new intraday high, before easing to HK$35.70.
Guangdong Investment added HK$0.30 to reach its new high of HK$6.00. The share then inched back to HK$5.85, up HK$0.10 from its previous high of HK$5.75.
